description:
The turbine's energy sink term must be SHAFT WORK, not a prescribed heat sink, and it must feed the rotor inertia ODE J domega/dt = T_turb - T_gen. Without that coupling the twin cannot do load rejection or overspeed, which is the transient a turbine twin exists for.

ThreePhaseElectricGeneratorTurbine (tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/generator.rs) is a working lumped electromechanical rotor — torque balance, omega, EMF, current, power — but it takes torque as a FREE INPUT and has no steam path. This bead closes that loop: steam expansion supplies the torque.

Two design constraints from the 2026-08-04 review:
- Do NOT give the turbine CV real blade-path fluid inventory. Steam residence time is milliseconds; a CV with true blade volume adds a stiff acoustic mode that shrinks the timestep for no physics. Model the turbine as a quasi-steady junction (flow law + work extraction) between volumes, with storage in the steam chest and adjacent pipes. If the CV has volume, it represents the chest/casing.
- Casing heat loss is a genuine SECOND sink but is small (order 0.5-1 percent) — optional.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 1.
title: tampines Turbine: couple the shaft-work sink to rotor inertia and the generator
